note: How many crew must be on the clock at once for a unit-shift to count as a
unit that ran. UHU's denominator is unit hours actually crewed, so a
profile rostered with one person contributes nothing -- which is the point:
anything but a wheelchair or secure car needs two, a licensed clinician
plus someone to drive.
default_min_crew applies to every profile with no matching pattern.
by_pattern maps a case-insensitive substring of the shift profile name to
the crew that profile needs, longest pattern first.
The patterns below match this tenant's naming convention, where the second
segment of a profile name carries the vehicle class:
A   ambulance     OH-A-CIN-(12)-06-19, IN-A-SBG-07-19    two crew
S   secure car    OH-S-CBUS-SC 1, OH-S-CIN-(4)-06-18     one crew
SC  secure car    OH-SC-MAS-06-19 (1)                    one crew
W   wheelchair    OH-W-MAS-07-20 (1), WV-W-PAR-07-17     one crew
Wheelchair also appears spelled out as a suffix -- 'WV-BER-07-17 W/C',
'WV-CHAR-WC-08-18', 'INDY WC' -- so W/C and WC are matched too.
Admin rosters and supervisor trucks need two, the same as any ambulance:
they count toward UHU only when two people are actually on them. Both are
listed explicitly rather than left to default_min_crew, so the decision
survives a change to that default.
Match the words as well as the codes, so a profile named in full still
resolves if the convention is ever dropped.
The Staffing report reads this same file, so a unit short of its own
minimum is marked SHORT there rather than dropped.
Rename to unit_staffing_rules.json to put it in effect. Verify with
probe_uhu_sources.py: it writes unit_staffing_rules.proposed.json listing
every profile it saw with the crew it was scored as.
